summary: In-gun Kang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under several scholars, and earned a doctorate at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes.

Ines Konczak specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.
Ingmar Heise focuses on Sinology and Buddhist studies. Heise earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Strauch earned a PhD at the Free University of Berlin by 2000, taught Kathrin Holz, and served as Professeur at the University of Lausanne, attested in 2018.
Inyoung Chung is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner, attested in 2008.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Free University of Brussels, Harvard University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Tibet University, and taught anthropology at Laval University around 2004 and 2007.
Isabelle Onians works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Isabelle Ratié is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Paris 1, EPHE, and under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, University of Paris, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).
Isaline Blew Horner was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Newnham College around 1914–1917 and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society from circa 1942 to 1958.
Iselin Frydenlund works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she was attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo and as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School and Sanskrit College and University, where he later served as Direttore from around 1851 to 1858.
Issaen Ikeyama, a scholar in Buddhist studies, held posts as professor (教授) at both Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.
Issei Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later held a post there as professor (教授).
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Sophia University and a master's course (修士課程) at Aichi Gakuin University.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1871–1890) and taught Sergey Oldenburg and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.
Ives Waldo worked in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988, and taught David P. Jackson.
Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan works in Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.
Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at Charles University in 1960 and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology in 1970.

Iwao Nakajima earned a master's degree from Hitotsubashi University and studied under Nichiki Kimura. Nakajima held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and as chief editor (主幹) at Sandhaan, attested in 1999.

Iwao Shima was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University (~1969–1978). He held posts at Kanazawa University from around 1986 to 1995, and as professor (教授) from around 1995 to 2007.
